cases.purpose: Invoke the bashclear entry point on a controlling PTY and check bytes, termios and window-size preservation.
cases.oracle: ncurses clear with matching arguments and the same terminal state. Python TIOCGWINSZ independently reads the window dimensions before and after.
cases.comparison: Exact raw PTY bytes against clear; independent unchanged winsize predicate and full termios restoration.
cases.candidate_script: before=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import fcntl,termios;print(fcntl.ioctl(0,termios.TIOCGWINSZ,b"\0"*8).hex())'); bashclear ; rc=$?; after=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import fcntl,termios;print(fcntl.ioctl(0,termios.TIOCGWINSZ,b"\0"*8).hex())'); [[ $before == "$after" ]] && echo unchanged > winsize || echo changed > winsize; exit "$rc"
cases.reference_script: before=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import fcntl,termios;print(fcntl.ioctl(0,termios.TIOCGWINSZ,b"\0"*8).hex())'); clear ; rc=$?; after=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import fcntl,termios;print(fcntl.ioctl(0,termios.TIOCGWINSZ,b"\0"*8).hex())'); [[ $before == "$after" ]] && echo unchanged > winsize || echo changed > winsize; exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check tty against the actual stdin terminal path, including the terminating newline, and require tty -s to return 0 without output.
cases.oracle: GNU tty and Python os.ttyname(0) on the same private slave; raw name bytes are checked before conversion to a fixed marker.
cases.comparison: Independently verified exact pathname bytes; full raw PTY output has only the verifier/status markers, so silent mode cannot emit unnoticed bytes.
cases.script:
tty > name; first=$?
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os,pathlib;assert pathlib.Path("name").read_bytes()==os.fsencode(os.ttyname(0))+bytes([10]);print("name=exact")' || exit 90
rm -f name
tty -s; quiet=$?; printf "status=%s,%s\n" "$first" "$quiet"

cases.purpose: Observe the status and diagnostic after an ENOSPC write and verify output from the same shell afterwards.
cases.oracle: ncurses clear; trusted setup independently proves the guest /dev/full produces ENOSPC.
cases.comparison: Exact observed status and diagnostic bytes, plus continued shell output.

cases.purpose: Force a four-byte partial clear write at a 1024-byte file-size limit, then EFBIG; compare status/diagnostic and shell continuation.
cases.oracle: ncurses clear -T vt100; the known ESC[H ESC[J sequence crosses the file-size limit after four bytes. Bash ignores SIGXFSZ for this bounded child shell.
cases.comparison: Exact resulting 1024 bytes, diagnostic tree, status and subsequent output; the size limit is confined to the disposable subshell.
cases.script: ( trap "" XFSZ; ulimit -f 1; clear -T vt100 >> short.out 2> diagnostic; printf "status=%s\n" "$?"; printf "recovered\n" )

cases.purpose: Run clear with stdout on a hung-up PTY (verified EIO), then restore stdout and print from the same shell.
cases.oracle: ncurses clear on an independently created private PTY; Python verifies EIO before either implementation runs.
cases.comparison: Exact error diagnostics and recorded clear status against ncurses; the recovery file proves the invoking shell continues after restoring its output.
